problem_text:
A logistics company is selecting cargo containers to load onto a delivery truck. Available containers are:
* Container 1: weight 30kg, revenue 144 dollars
* Container 2: weight 23kg, revenue 152 dollars
* Container 3: weight 40kg, revenue 123 dollars
* Container 4: weight 46kg, revenue 103 dollars
* Container 5: weight 36kg, revenue 242 dollars
* Container 6: weight 30kg, revenue 142 dollars
* Container 7: weight 31kg, revenue 58 dollars
* Container 8: weight 6kg, revenue 98 dollars
* Container 9: weight 36kg, revenue 36 dollars
* Container 10: weight 50kg, revenue 138 dollars
* Container 11: weight 24kg, revenue 180 dollars
* Container 12: weight 24kg, revenue 39 dollars
* Container 13: weight 25kg, revenue 184 dollars
* Container 14: weight 12kg, revenue 155 dollars
* Container 15: weight 31kg, revenue 32 dollars
* Container 16: weight 35kg, revenue 268 dollars
* Container 17: weight 20kg, revenue 173 dollars
* Container 18: weight 18kg, revenue 173 dollars
* Container 19: weight 5kg, revenue 188 dollars
* Container 20: weight 2kg, revenue 239 dollars
* Container 21: weight 40kg, revenue 98 dollars
* Container 22: weight 23kg, revenue 160 dollars
* Container 23: weight 45kg, revenue 145 dollars
The truck has a maximum payload capacity of 442 kg. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
